rationale:
This edition brings an over-budget incumbent within the reader's budget. It restates the judgment rather than changing it. The article is retold within its ceiling. The assessment is rewritten within every field ceiling: the dossier header, research priority, synthesis, steelman, best conventional explanation, component notes, and a complete treatment for each featured claim. The case verdict (unresolved), the load-bearing set, the weakest links and the component states are unchanged.

One claim verdict changes. ORCH-C046, the LISA Pathfinder bound, goes from well_supported to unresolved with low confidence. The ledger has no admitted evidence record attached to that claim. The same bound enters the case only as ORCH-E046, which is attached to the collapse-physics claim ORCH-C030. The rule for claims held on their source statement alone therefore applies. The bound is still weighed where its record is attached, in the physics component and the synthesis.

The article now tells ORCH-C046 and ORCH-C057 as reports rather than as findings. It also drops a proposition the incumbent stated in the page's voice: that a published radical-pair model reproduces the four xenon potencies. The records carrying that proposition were refused at intake. The article now says only that radical-pair researchers took up the same four numbers (a restatement in the ledger), and treats field dependence as that account's natural prediction.

The article no longer uses the ledger's vocabulary ('rungs', 'ladder'). It no longer narrates the xenon regression in statistical detail, and it compresses the collapse-physics escape into one paragraph. The detail of the MRI reply, the AI-mathematics error history and the editor's-view box has gone to the claim pages.

Selection and crux order are otherwise unchanged. The featured set remains the map of the controversy: the thesis, its four load-bearing claims, each competing account, and the observations on which they turn.

Two research items are settled. ORCH-R008 is answered by study ORCH-S001. ORCH-R010 is answered by study ORCH-S002.

The article's prose groups the six accounts exactly as the accounts field does.
article:
Orch OR, the theory of Roger Penrose and Stuart Hameroff, proposes that [each conscious moment is a gravity-triggered collapse of a quantum state spread across tubulin proteins in neuronal microtubules]{claim=ORCH-C001}, and that anesthetics work by breaking that state. The evidence so far splits cleanly. Microtubules turn out to be electronically and optically livelier than a passive scaffold should be, and anesthetics measurably perturb them. But nobody has measured the thing the theory needs: quantum coherence lasting tens of milliseconds in a warm brain. Meanwhile the simplest version of Penrose's collapse physics has been ruled out underground. The theory stands unresolved. It is not refuted, because its central quantity has never been measured. It is not supported, because nothing yet measured is that quantity. What remains open is a short list of experiments, almost none of them run.

## Five claims, not one

Arguments about Orch OR usually slide between five different things:

- quantum effects in microtubules;
- quantum coherence in microtubules;
- entanglement across microtubules;
- quantum computation in neurons;
- Penrose's gravitational collapse.

The first is trivially true, since all chemistry is quantum. The last is an open proposal in the foundations of physics. Evidence for one is not evidence for the next.

Keeping them apart produces verdicts that look odd until you see why. That [microtubules have collective electronic behaviour a passive scaffold would not show]{claim=ORCH-C013} is well supported. That [they hold coherent quantum states long enough and widely enough for the theory's computation]{claim=ORCH-C010} is unresolved: not contradicted, but unmeasured. The headline needs both, and cannot rise above the weaker of the two.

## What microtubules actually do

{plate:IMG-ORCHOR-P01}

The pivotal experiment comes from Gregory Scholes's ultrafast spectroscopy laboratory at Princeton. The group watches how tryptophan fluorescence changes as a quencher is added. From that it infers that [electronic excitation travels about 6.6 nanometres through polymerized microtubules, further than standard energy-transfer theory accounts for, and that the anesthetics etomidate and isoflurane shorten that distance]{claim=ORCH-C020}. Their own summary is that microtubules are, unexpectedly, effective light harvesters. Hameroff and Penrose are among the co-authors, so this is a collaboration that includes the theory's originators, not an outside test.

A partly independent group at Howard University reports that [fluorescence efficiency rises as tubulin is organized into larger structures, as a model of collective 'superradiant' tryptophan states predicts]{claim=ORCH-C021}. A 2026 measurement in pig tubulin reproduces the direction of that rise at 280 nanometres. Microtubules are not inert beams, and that is worth knowing whatever anyone thinks about consciousness.

Now the limits. 6.6 nanometres is roughly one tubulin dimer, the unit pictured above, and the physics runs in femtoseconds to picoseconds. Orch OR needs milliseconds, across many tubulins.

The superradiance work's striking figure is collective states with radiative lifetimes of 'tens of seconds'. That measures how weakly a state couples to light, not how long it survives jostling by its surroundings. A state can stay dark for seconds and still lose its coherence in femtoseconds. The newest modelling of the same geometry defines its lifetimes within a radiation-only model, with no water, ions or molecular vibrations in it. Its authors write that their results do not imply microtubules must use quantum correlations for neural processing at all.

The optical signal itself is not yet stable. Microtubules scatter ultraviolet light strongly. In the 2026 dataset, the polymerization effect at 280 nanometres ranges from about +6% to about +47%, depending on which of two defensible scattering corrections is used. At 295 nanometres the two corrections disagree on the sign: about −59% on one and about +13% on the other. That is the wavelength that excites tryptophan most selectively, and so where comparison with a tryptophan model means most.

The same modellers report that [adding realistic structural disorder sharply cuts the collective enhancement relative to an idealized lattice]{claim=ORCH-C063}. What survives is a modest yield trend, not the large cooperative effect an argument from molecules to brains needs. Anyone who correlates this signal with anesthetic potency before fixing the scattering problem risks measuring the correction rather than the physics.

What would settle the central question is a coherence time measured at body temperature. What exists instead is two calculations. Max Tegmark puts microtubule decoherence at 10⁻¹³ to 10⁻²⁰ seconds, against neural timescales of 10⁻³ to 10⁻¹ seconds. Hagan, Hameroff and Tuszyński reply that he modelled the wrong physical state, and get 10⁻⁵ to 10⁻⁴ seconds instead. That is still two to three orders of magnitude short of the roughly 25-millisecond conscious moment the theory names.

This site's survey of the theory's own literature finds its numbers consistent for two decades. It finds no published pass/fail threshold for any direct coherence test. It also finds a change of physical carrier in 2014, from protein shape changes to collective dipoles, so results against the old mechanism no longer bear on the new one.

Anirban Bandyopadhyay's group in Japan offers what it presents as the bridge from molecules to brains: [self-similar 'triplet of triplet' resonance patterns in tubulin, in microtubules, and in part of a neuron]{claim=ORCH-C022}. Resonance is a classical observable, so even a real pattern would not show coherence. No outside laboratory has reproduced it in more than a decade.

## The anesthesia experiments, in both directions

{plate:IMG-ORCHOR-P02}

This is the part of the case that can be tested now, and it has a real empirical fight in it.

The evidence for starts with the finding that [anesthetics bind tubulin and change microtubule photophysics]{claim=ORCH-C011}. An anesthesia laboratory at Penn with no stake in the theory finds that an anthracene anesthetic photolabels β-tubulin. The same laboratory finds that microtubule stabilizers raise the dose needed to immobilize tadpoles.

Then comes the behavioural result from Wellesley: [a single dose of the stabilizer epothilone B delays isoflurane-induced loss of the righting reflex by 69 seconds in rats and 29 seconds in mice]{claim=ORCH-C023}. The rat study is blinded, controls for tolerance and reports a large effect, but it uses eight male rats. The mouse study comes from the same laboratory, and it calls its own effect modest against the variation between animals.

The evidence against comes from an independent group at Massachusetts General Hospital. It runs a randomized, blinded study with full dose–response curves. It finds that [two weeks of the stabilizer epothilone D makes mice more sensitive to isoflurane, and the destabilizer vinblastine does the same]{claim=ORCH-C024}. No account based on microtubule stability predicts a stabilizer and a destabilizer acting alike; general cellular disruption would.

The drug and the dosing schedule differ, so this does not refute the acute result. It does undo the idea that [manipulating microtubule stability changes anesthetic susceptibility]{claim=ORCH-C012} in any consistent direction. The Wellesley group, to its credit, cites the contrary study in its own abstract.

The sharpest objection comes from inside the Princeton experiment. It also tests picrotoxin, a convulsant and pharmacologically the opposite of an anesthetic, and reports a comparable effect on the same assay. If a convulsant and two anesthetics all move the signal, the assay may be measuring how easily small oily molecules perturb microtubule photophysics, not anything specific to anesthesia.

A test that would decide this is well defined. It needs eight or more agents, including non-anesthetics matched for solubility, free drug concentrations measured, and the predicted correlation registered in advance. It has not been run.

## A quantum anomaly that points elsewhere

One result is genuinely strange: [xenon isotopes that carry nuclear spin are weaker anesthetics than spin-zero isotopes, although their calculated polarizability is identical]{claim=ORCH-C025}. It comes from a randomized study of 80 mice published in *Anesthesiology*. Nuclear spin is a quantum property, and there is no classical-chemistry explanation to hand.

This site's own re-analysis of the four published groups finds the shape of the pattern striking. One mass unit across the spin boundary changes potency by about 30 points; two mass units within a spin pair change it by a few. A smooth effect of mass cannot produce a step like that.

The same re-analysis finds the result thinner than its citation record suggests:

- the headline xenon-alone values are calculated from mixtures with isoflurane, not measured directly;
- the error bars are of unstated type;
- the data cannot statistically separate spin from mass;
- in eight years nobody has repeated the experiment.

Spin also points at some spin-sensitive chemistry, not at microtubules. Researchers proposing radical-pair chemistry, in which the spins of paired electrons steer a reaction, have taken up those same four numbers. The same group models the idea that [a magnetically sensitive radical pair modulates how fast microtubules assemble]{claim=ORCH-C044}. That is a parameter fit, not a measurement. But it offers a mechanism for chemically opposite microtubule drugs acting alike. Any radical-pair account implies a cheap test nobody has run: does the xenon isotope effect change with magnetic field?

## The physics, tested underground

Penrose's contribution stands apart from the biology. He proposes that [superpositions of sufficiently different mass distributions collapse on their own, with a lifetime set by the gravitational self-energy of the difference]{claim=ORCH-C030}: τ ≈ ℏ/E_G. Physicists test this for their own reasons.

If gravity collapses wavefunctions in the standard random way, charged particles should faintly emit X-rays. A team including Lajos Diósi, co-originator of the model, looked with an ultra-low-background germanium detector under Gran Sasso. They [found nothing, ruling out 'the natural parameter-free version of the Diósi–Penrose model']{claim=ORCH-C031}. The independent [Majorana Demonstrator found no such radiation either, in 37.5 kilogram-years of enriched germanium]{claim=ORCH-C047}. These are the best-designed experiments in the case, and both are negative.

The philosopher Kelvin McQueen presses an escape: Penrose's criterion is a lifetime rule, not a random-noise equation, and predicts no radiation. That is correct, and it is why this claim is unresolved rather than refuted. But the escape is getting costly, for three reasons.

- A reanalysis of LISA Pathfinder data reports that [the spacecraft's measured acceleration noise between free-falling test masses forces the model's cutoff length above the size of any nucleus]{claim=ORCH-C046}. That is a mechanical channel, and an argument about radiation does not reach it.
- Diósi reports that [a construction he developed with Tilloy reproduces Penrose's rate exactly]{claim=ORCH-C066}. So 'the tested model was never Penrose's' becomes a question of which dynamics. Whether that particular dynamics is already excluded is a calculation someone could do at a desk.
- Diósi writes that the rate carries an unspecified constant, and that [he and Penrose agree on the collapse time but disagree on how collapse happens]{claim=ORCH-C069}.

The lifetime rule itself is untested, and every dynamics proposed to realize it is being squeezed.

## The living-brain signal

One experiment claims to see non-classical behaviour directly. [Zero-quantum-coherence MRI of living human brains picks up heartbeat-timed signals that depend on conscious awareness, which the experimenters read as witnessing entanglement]{claim=ORCH-C026}. Subjects report the signal fading as they fall asleep.

Warren S. Warren, a leading NMR methodologist, replies that the data show only that living tissue is complex and imprecisely characterized by MRI. The authors answer with numbers. The classical mechanism he proposes, they calculate, could reach at most 0.4% of the initial magnetization, or 0.13% once relaxation is included, far below what they observe. That answers one classical explanation, but in the authors' own words and with formulas derived for chemical solutions. Nobody else has run the sequence.

Even fully validated, the result would implicate no microtubule: the known quantum systems in the measurement are the spins of protons in water.

## The argument that started it

Penrose came to microtubules from Gödel. His argument, in its weaker form, is that [human mathematical understanding is not the execution of any knowably sound algorithm]{claim=ORCH-C040}. If that is so, something in the brain's physics must be non-computable.

Machines now press on the argument. [An AI model has disproved a 1946 Erdős conjecture, confirmed and improved by an independent mathematician, and AI systems have reached Lean-verified silver and officially graded gold at the International Mathematical Olympiad]{claim=ORCH-C041}.

The Penrose-side reply is that these are results inside existing frameworks, not the invention of new ones. A co-author of DeepMind's AlphaProof argues much the same in a position paper: the systems deduce, but cannot make the jump to new premises. The case editor's own essay concedes that Penrose's testable examples have mostly gone against him. It defends 'the escalator, not the steps', and leaves open whether that is depth or unfalsifiability.

**This bears on why the theory was proposed, not on whether it is true.** Refute the Gödel argument and every microtubule claim stands where it was. Vindicate it and microtubules gain no special claim to be what does the non-computing.

## The live accounts, side by side

- **Orch OR.** Predicts coherence at 37 °C lasting tens of milliseconds, anesthetic suppression of it that scales with clinical potency, and collapse lifetimes that scale as ℏ/E_G.
- **Interesting condensed matter, nothing more.** Predicts coherence lost within femtoseconds to picoseconds, optical effects moved by any small oily molecule (convulsants included), and no potency correlation.
- **Classical multi-target pharmacology.** Predicts that receptor genetics keeps explaining the drugs one by one, and that microtubule drugs act through transport, metabolism and cell health.
- **Spin chemistry without microtubules.** Predicts that the xenon isotope effect changes with magnetic field, and that isotope or redox manipulations shift microtubule assembly.
- **Non-classical brain, other site.** Predicts that the MRI signal replicates in other hands and survives tests on calibrated phantoms, with no dependence on microtubules.
- **Collapse physics on its own.** Predicts that ℏ/E_G scaling shows up, or fails to, in levitated-particle or condensate experiments, whatever the brain does.

## The conventional account, taken seriously

On anesthesia, the conventional account has causal evidence Orch OR lacks. [A single engineered change in the GABA_A receptor β3 subunit abolishes the immobilizing action of etomidate and propofol and sharply reduces their hypnotic effect]{claim=ORCH-C003}. Change one amino acid, and the drug stops working. Nothing comparable exists for tubulin.

Its limits are the proponents' opening. The same mutation barely affects volatile anesthetics, which its authors conclude act through a broader set of targets. The hypnotic effect is reduced, not abolished. A review by senior anesthesia researchers reports that two decades of work found no channel, and no combination of channels, sufficient for immobility under inhaled agents. So [the stronger claim that anesthesia and cognition are *fully* classical]{claim=ORCH-C004} is unresolved.

The proponents' best argument sits here. Proponent quantum-chemical modelling reportedly predicts several volatile agents' potencies from how they bind to tubulin. In effect it reproduces the Meyer–Overton correlation, anesthesiology's oldest rule, which links a drug's potency to its solubility in oil. A proponent commentary asserts that [no other candidate target has a published model that does the same]{claim=ORCH-C057}. That assertion has no survey behind it, and the modelling has never been tested prospectively. But no rival model is on the table either.

The conventional account also gives no principled story of why any of this activity is experienced. Orch OR attempts one, but attempting an explanation is not evidence for it.

## What would settle it

- **A coherence measurement in microtubules at 37 °C**, against a pass/fail threshold proponents publish in advance. A clean null near the requirement would close the biological half. Tens of milliseconds would be a landmark in biophysics.
- **A stable optical signal.** Fix the scattering ambiguity first. Then run an anesthetic potency series that includes non-anesthetic and convulsant controls. A slope that tracks clinical potency would be hard to explain conventionally.
- **A tubulin knock-in mouse** that cannot bind anesthetic but still builds normal microtubules, with receptor function checked unchanged. This is the only design that would give the microtubule idea causal evidence of the receptor account's quality.
- **A preregistered multicentre epothilone replication**, with acute and chronic dosing side by side and brain drug levels measured.
- **A direct test of ℏ/E_G scaling** in mesoscopic superpositions, plus the desk calculation of whether the one dynamics known to give Penrose's rate is already excluded.
- **A magnetic-field test of the xenon isotope effect.** If the effect shifts with the field, the anomaly belongs to spin chemistry, not microtubules.

None of these requires believing the theory first, and almost none has been run.

researchStatus.note: Study ORCH-S001 collected the corpus. ORCH-E035 shows the theory's parameter values are consistent across two decades, that no pass/fail threshold for any direct coherence test is published, and that the carrier changed in 2014. ORCH-E036 shows no unconditional proponent estimate reaches 25 ms. The remaining step, a proponent-endorsed threshold fixed in advance, is carried by the open item ORCH-R014.

Study ORCH-S002 ran the pre-registered two-covariate re-analysis. ORCH-E037: the frozen identification rule tripped (condition number 302.4, driven by the narrow mass range rather than spin–mass collinearity), so no spin coefficient is evidential. ORCH-E038: a spin step describes the four means far better than a linear mass term, descriptively only. ORCH-E039 and ORCH-E040: the result is unreplicated, its headline values are calculated, and its dispersions are of unstated type. The dataset cannot support the inferential test; a new experiment (ORCH-R011) is what remains.

assessment.synthesis:
Orch OR is a conjunction — gravitational collapse (ORCH-C030), a millisecond microtubule quantum state (ORCH-C010), and their identity with experience (ORCH-C001) — and is unresolved because its weakest conjunct is unmeasured.

The observations are respectable. ORCH-E001 and ORCH-E004 show microtubules are electronically and optically collective (ORCH-C013). ORCH-E056 reproduces the direction of the quantum-yield trend (ORCH-C021), but ORCH-E075 through ORCH-E079 show that trend's size, and at 295 nm its sign, depend on the scattering correction. None of this is a coherence time. On ORCH-C010, ORCH-E036 shows no unconditional proponent estimate reaches the theory's own 25 ms; ORCH-E035 finds no published pass/fail threshold; and ORCH-E072 and ORCH-E073 show the newest modelling reports radiative, not dephasing, lifetimes.

The physics conjunct is squeezed. Two underground nulls (ORCH-E017, ORCH-E049) exclude the parameter-free stochastic model (ORCH-C031). ORCH-E046, on ORCH-C030, bounds the cutoff through mechanical noise, a channel the no-radiation escape (ORCH-E019) does not reach. ORCH-C030 stays unresolved because ORCH-E071 records the rate's constant as unspecified, and because the dynamics is what the originators dispute (ORCH-C069, per ORCH-E052).

On anesthesia (ORCH-C002), a convulsant moves the flagship assay (ORCH-E003). The best independent animal study finds a stabilizer and a destabilizer both increasing sensitivity (ORCH-E013). The xenon result (ORCH-C025) is unreplicated and rests on calculated headline values (ORCH-E039, ORCH-E040), and it implicates spin chemistry rather than microtubules.

Sensitivity: removing ORCH-E013 would most change the case, lifting ORCH-C012 from mixed and cleaning up the anesthesia arm. The case verdict would survive, because it rests on an absence — no coherence or dephasing time has ever been measured in a microtubule — and no single record removes an absence.
assessment.steelman:
The strongest unanswered argument is Meyer–Overton. The correlation between anesthetic potency and lipid solubility is anesthesiology's oldest quantitative regularity. Proponent quantum-chemical modelling reportedly predicts several volatile agents' potencies from binding to tubulin's delocalized electrons (ORCH-E010, restated at ORCH-E084 to ORCH-E086, all on ORCH-C011). Proponents assert that no other candidate target has a published model that does the same (ORCH-C057, held on a commentary's sentence alone).

Set beside that two admissions from the rival side. Eger and colleagues report that two decades of work found no channel, or combination, sufficient for immobility under inhaled agents (ORCH-E031, on ORCH-C004). The β3 receptor result's own authors conclude that volatile agents act through a broader set of targets (ORCH-E015, on ORCH-C003). On the proponents' reading, for the inhaled agents most of this literature uses, the one structure modelled to reproduce the field's founding regularity is the one Orch OR names, while the rival concedes it has no sufficient target.

This assessment discounts the argument because the modelling is computational and proponent-authored, the uniqueness claim has no survey behind it, and a convulsant moves the related optical assay (ORCH-E003). But no refuting survey and no rival target-level model exists either.
assessment.whatIsClaimed: That each conscious moment is a gravity-induced collapse of a quantum state spread across tubulin proteins in neuronal microtubules, and that anesthetics abolish consciousness by breaking that state. The collapse is Penrose's objective reduction, timed by τ ≈ ℏ/E_G; the rival view holds that receptors, channels and circuits suffice.
assessment.whereDisagreementLives: In one unmeasured gap: microtubules demonstrably move electronic energy about one tubulin dimer within picoseconds, but nobody has measured the millisecond-long, many-tubulin coherent state the theory needs. The theory has never published the threshold that would make such a measurement pass or fail. On the physics side, the live question is whether any dynamics reproducing Penrose's rate survives the underground radiation and spacecraft acceleration-noise limits.
assessment.whatWouldSettleIt: Measuring how long quantum coherence actually lasts in microtubules at body temperature, against a pass/fail threshold proponents publish in advance, would settle the biological half. An anesthetic potency series against the optical signal counts only once its scattering ambiguity is closed. A tubulin knock-in mouse that cannot bind anesthetic would give causal evidence. The physics needs its own test of whether collapse lifetimes scale as ℏ/E_G.
assessment.bestConventionalExplanation: Classical neural computation: cognition lives in membrane potentials, synapses and network dynamics, and consciousness is an organizational property of that activity, not a quantum event. For anesthesia, the account is multi-target pharmacology, with causal evidence Orch OR lacks. One point mutation in the GABA_A receptor β3 subunit abolishes the immobilizing action of etomidate and propofol and sharply reduces their hypnotic effect, while volatile agents act on a broader set of targets. On this account the microtubule findings are ordinary physics and cell biology. An ordered aromatic lattice has collective photophysics whether or not anything computes with it. Small hydrophobic molecules, convulsants included, perturb it. Microtubule drugs shift anesthetic sensitivity through transport, metabolism and cell health, which is the natural reading of a stabilizer and a destabilizer acting alike. Its acknowledged gaps are that it offers no account of why any of this is experienced, and no sufficient molecular target for inhaled agents.

components.label: Collective electronic and optical behaviour of microtubules
components.note: Measured in more than one laboratory, though the size of the main optical effect depends on how light scattering is corrected. This is physics of an ordered lattice, not computation.

components.label: Quantum coherence lasting a conscious moment
components.note: Never measured. Two calculations differ by eight orders of magnitude or more, and the proponents' own best unconditional estimate falls short of their 25 ms requirement.

components.label: Anesthesia by breaking a microtubule quantum state
components.note: Anesthetics do affect tubulin and animal latency. But a convulsant moves the same assay, the best independent study runs the other way, and no quantum variable was measured.

components.label: Gravitational collapse as physics
components.note: Two underground experiments exclude the simplest version, and a spacecraft noise limit tightens the squeeze. Penrose's lifetime rule itself is untested, and how collapse happens is still disputed.

components.label: Non-classical signals in the living brain
components.note: A consciousness-linked MRI signal whose authors answered the proposed classical explanation. Nobody else has reproduced it, and it implicates no microtubule.

components.label: The non-computability motivation
components.note: Machines now produce verified new mathematics, while the reply about inventing frameworks stands. Either way this bears on why the theory was proposed, not on microtubules.

researchPriority.reason: The case turns on one quantity never measured — microtubule coherence at body temperature — and the measurement is within reach of existing ultrafast spectroscopy. Two cheap desk tasks and one measurement fix should come first.

claimAssessments.reasoning: The headline conjunction depends on ORCH-C010 and ORCH-C030, both unresolved. ORCH-E007 (a calculation) and ORCH-E016 (an unread commentary) undermine it. ORCH-E018 applies the Gran Sasso bound, but only conditionally. ORCH-E035 shows no pass/fail threshold was ever published. ORCH-E028 and ORCH-E055 are context only. It is not contradicted, because neither conjunct has been measured against a threshold. It is not supported, because no record touches the identity of collapse with experience.

treatment.plainLanguage: Each moment of awareness is a gravity-triggered collapse of a quantum state inside brain microtubules.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: This is the thesis itself; every other claim is graded by how it bears here.
treatment.strongestObjection: Warm, wet tissue should destroy quantum coherence long before 25 ms, and no measurement says otherwise (ORCH-E007).
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A coherence measurement at 37 °C reaching tens of milliseconds against a threshold published in advance
A clean null near the theory's requirement under physiological conditions
A mesoscopic experiment confirming or excluding ℏ/E_G collapse scaling

claimAssessments.reasoning: ORCH-E002, ORCH-E011 and ORCH-E014 show three things: anesthetics perturb microtubule photophysics, a stabilizer delays unconsciousness in one laboratory, and nuclear spin matters for xenon. None measures a quantum state. Against the claim stand the convulsant control (ORCH-E003), the independent opposite-direction study (ORCH-E013) and the receptor mutation (ORCH-E015). ORCH-E029 records that the claimed independent confirmations do not hold.

treatment.plainLanguage: Anesthetics switch off consciousness mainly by breaking a quantum state in microtubules.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: If shown, this would single out the microtubule account over classical pharmacology; the current records do not discriminate.
treatment.strongestObjection: A single receptor mutation abolishes intravenous anesthetic action (ORCH-E015); nothing comparable exists for tubulin.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A potency series in which suppression of a microtubule signal tracks clinical potency while nonimmobilizers fail
A tubulin binding-site knock-in mouse that resists anesthesia with receptor function unchanged
A preregistered multicentre replication of the epothilone results

claimAssessments.reasoning: ORCH-E015 is target-level causal evidence: the β3(N265M) mutation abolishes etomidate and propofol immobility and sharply reduces hypnosis. ORCH-E030 qualifies it, since hypnosis is reduced rather than abolished. The claim is worded as 'substantially accounted for', with target-specific evidence for intravenous agents only, so both records fit it.

treatment.plainLanguage: Anesthesia is largely explained by drugs acting on receptors and ion channels in the brain.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Strong for intravenous agents, silent on the volatile agents most Orch OR experiments use.
treatment.strongestObjection: The same mutation barely touches volatile anesthetics, and the hypnosis endpoint is only partly removed (ORCH-E030).
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A tubulin knock-in producing anesthetic resistance comparable to β3(N265M)
Failure to reproduce the β3 behavioural dissociation

claimAssessments.reasoning: This is the exhaustive version of the classical account. ORCH-E031 reports no channel, or combination, sufficient for immobility under inhaled agents. ORCH-E030 shows the β3 mutation only partly removes hypnosis. ORCH-E033 is a weak dissociation between experience and blood flow. No record shows a quantum contribution either; the universal 'fully' is simply not established.

treatment.plainLanguage: Everything about anesthesia and thought is classical, with no quantum role at all.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: If established it would exclude Orch OR, but no record tests a universal negative.
treatment.strongestObjection: Not having named a sufficient target yet is ignorance, not evidence of a quantum mechanism.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A classical target or combination shown sufficient for volatile anesthesia
A replicated quantum-specific effect, such as field-dependent xenon isotope potency

claimAssessments.reasoning: ORCH-E017, with ORCH-E070 as context, excludes the parameter-free stochastic version. ORCH-E018 applies that result to Orch OR only conditionally. ORCH-E046 bounds the regularization length above any nuclear size through mechanical noise, which the no-radiation escape in ORCH-E019 does not reach. ORCH-E071 records the rate's constant as unspecified. The lifetime relation itself has never been tested directly, so it is not contradicted.

treatment.plainLanguage: Quantum superpositions of different mass arrangements collapse on their own, and faster the bigger the gravitational difference.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: A necessary conjunct of the thesis; refuting it sinks Orch OR whatever the biology shows.
treatment.strongestObjection: Every dynamics proposed to realize the rate is being squeezed, and the escape relies on the theory being less specified than what was tested.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A mesoscopic experiment measuring collapse lifetime against ℏ/E_G
A calculation showing the Tilloy–Diósi dynamics already excluded by existing bounds

claimAssessments.reasoning: ORCH-E022 and ORCH-E023 show machines producing verified novel mathematics, which weighs against the claim. ORCH-E025 argues the systems deduce but cannot form new premises. ORCH-E026 concedes Penrose's testable examples have mostly failed, while defending a version that cannot be tested. A claim about knowably sound algorithms is not settled by performance records.

treatment.plainLanguage: Human mathematical insight cannot be any provably reliable computer program.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Bears on why the theory was proposed, not on whether microtubules do anything.
treatment.strongestObjection: An argument that no possible achievement can touch has bought its safety with its content.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: AI systems originating a new mathematical framework that mathematicians adopt
A formal argument closing the gap between Gödel's theorems and claims about human reasoning

claimAssessments.reasoning: No measurement exists. ORCH-E007 calculates 10⁻¹³–10⁻²⁰ s; ORCH-E008 counters with 10⁻⁵–10⁻⁴ s. ORCH-E036 shows no unconditional proponent estimate reaches 25 ms, and ORCH-E035 finds no published threshold. ORCH-E072 and ORCH-E073 show the newest modelling gives radiative, not dephasing, lifetimes. ORCH-E081 to ORCH-E083 are assertion only. The calculations lean against the claim, but the quantity itself is unmeasured.

treatment.plainLanguage: Microtubules at body temperature hold quantum coherence for tens of milliseconds across many proteins.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: The quantity that decides the biological half; the rival accounts predict femtosecond-to-picosecond loss of coherence.
treatment.strongestObjection: Every estimate not resting on special assumptions falls orders of magnitude below the requirement (ORCH-E036).
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Ultrafast spectroscopy at 37 °C showing coherence approaching 25 ms
A 310 K dephasing prediction published in advance, which a measurement then passes or fails
Femtosecond coherence loss measured under physiological conditions

claimAssessments.reasoning: ORCH-E009, from an independent laboratory, finds an anesthetic photolabelling β-tubulin and stabilizers raising the immobilizing dose. ORCH-E002 shows etomidate and isoflurane shortening exciton diffusion. ORCH-E003 undermines the specificity of the effect, not the binding or the optical change itself. ORCH-E010 and ORCH-E084 to ORCH-E086 are modelling and commentary. The claim is modest and the records fit it, but they rest on few agents.

treatment.plainLanguage: Anesthetics bind to tubulin and change how microtubules handle light and electronic energy.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Also expected on the conventional account, since small hydrophobic molecules perturb many proteins.
treatment.strongestObjection: A convulsant produced a comparable effect on the same assay (ORCH-E003).
whatWouldChangeOurMind: An eight-agent potency series including nonimmobilizers and solubility-matched controls
Failure to reproduce the exciton-diffusion reduction

claimAssessments.reasoning: ORCH-E009, ORCH-E011 and ORCH-E012 show stabilizers shifting anesthetic sensitivity in tadpoles, rats and mice. ORCH-E013, independent and blinded with full curves, finds a chronic stabilizer and a destabilizer both increasing sensitivity. ORCH-E032 is a weak human surrogate, and ORCH-E029 notes the confirmations are not independent. Sensitivity does change in every study, but the direction does not cohere, so as evidence for a stability-based mechanism the line is mixed.

treatment.plainLanguage: Drugs that stabilize or destabilize microtubules change how easily animals are anesthetized.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: A consistent direction would favour a microtubule role; the observed incoherence favours generic cellular disruption.
treatment.strongestObjection: A destabilizer moving sensitivity the same way as a stabilizer points to generic disruption (ORCH-E013).
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A preregistered multicentre study testing acute and chronic dosing side by side, with brain drug levels measured

claimAssessments.reasoning: ORCH-E001 (6.6 nm diffusion beyond the Förster prediction) and ORCH-E004 (quantum-yield enhancement) are quantitative and partly independent. ORCH-E005 is weak and unreplicated. ORCH-E006 and ORCH-E074 are context. This is condensed-matter behaviour, well supported as such, and silent on how long any coherence lasts.

treatment.plainLanguage: Microtubules are not inert scaffolding: they move electronic energy and interact with light collectively.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Necessary for Orch OR but predicted equally by the 'interesting condensed matter' account.
treatment.strongestObjection: The key diffusion paper includes the theory's originators among its co-authors and has not been independently replicated.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: An independent failure to reproduce the 6.6 nm diffusion length
The quantum-yield trend vanishing once scattering is properly corrected

claimAssessments.reasoning: ORCH-E001 reports the 6.6 nm diffusion length and ORCH-E002 the anesthetic reduction, both from the abstract of one open-access paper in a strong journal. The finding is not independently replicated, and the specific reduced lengths come via a secondary relay. But the claim as stated is what the paper measured.

treatment.plainLanguage: In laboratory microtubules, light energy spreads about 6.6 nanometres, and two anesthetics shorten that distance.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: A diffusion length on picosecond physics, not a coherence time; it fits the condensed-matter account too.
treatment.strongestObjection: One laboratory, with the theory's authors as co-authors, and a convulsant has a comparable effect (ORCH-E003, attached to ORCH-C011).
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Independent replication with a different quenching protocol

claimAssessments.reasoning: ORCH-E004 and the cross-laboratory ORCH-E056 support the direction of the quantum-yield increase at 280 nm. But ORCH-E075 puts its size anywhere between +6% and +47% depending on the correction chosen. ORCH-E076 to ORCH-E079 show the sign reversing at the tryptophan-selective 295 nm. The direction is real at one wavelength; the fit to the superradiance model is not yet testable.

treatment.plainLanguage: Organized tubulin glows more efficiently, as a model of collective light emission predicts.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Collective optics fits both Orch OR and the condensed-matter account; it says nothing about coherence duration.
treatment.strongestObjection: Scattering corrections alone move the effect from small to large, and flip its sign at 295 nm.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Cuvette and integrating-sphere measurements fixing a single value and sign at 280 and 295 nm

claimAssessments.reasoning: One weak record, ORCH-E005, from a single laboratory in a low-profile venue, unreplicated for years. Resonance is a classical observable, so even if real it would not show coherence.

treatment.plainLanguage: Tubulin, microtubules and neurons share repeating resonance patterns across very different scales.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Offered as the bridge from molecules to brains, but classical and unreplicated.
treatment.strongestObjection: Bespoke apparatus and no independent replication in more than a decade.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Independent laboratory replication with raw data and blinded analysis

claimAssessments.reasoning: ORCH-E011 (rats, blinded, tolerance control, d = 1.9) and ORCH-E012 (mice, d = 0.8, same laboratory) support the stated latencies. ORCH-E029 records that the two studies are not independent. The rat study has N = 8, males only, and no counterbalanced crossover. The observation is credible; what it means is not established.

treatment.plainLanguage: A single dose of a microtubule-stabilizing drug makes rodents take longer to pass out under isoflurane.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Predicted by Orch OR, but also by the drug's effects on transport or metabolism.
treatment.strongestObjection: The same laboratory twice; the only independent study found the opposite direction with a related drug.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Independent replication of acute epothilone B with brain drug levels measured
Failure to replicate in a counterbalanced design

claimAssessments.reasoning: ORCH-E013 quotes EC50 shifts with tight confidence intervals from a randomized, blinded, independent study. Its limits — chronic dosing, a saline vehicle, blood-gas changes — bear on interpretation, not on whether the shift was observed.

treatment.plainLanguage: Two weeks of a microtubule stabilizer made mice more sensitive to isoflurane, and so did a destabilizer.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Strains any stability-based mechanism; fits generic disruption or a spin-chemistry route.
treatment.strongestObjection: Chronic dosing invites compensation, and the compound differs from the acute studies.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Acute and chronic arms in one protocol showing that the dosing schedule explains the reversal

claimAssessments.reasoning: ORCH-E014 reports spin-bearing isotopes as weaker at equal polarizability. ORCH-E038 shows, descriptively, that a spin step fits the four means far better than mass. But ORCH-E039 finds no replication in eight years, and ORCH-E040 finds the headline values calculated and the dispersions of unstated type. ORCH-E037 shows the data cannot support a two-covariate test. ORCH-E034 and ORCH-E042 are context.

treatment.plainLanguage: Xenon atoms carrying nuclear spin are weaker anesthetics than otherwise identical atoms without it.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Implicates some spin-sensitive process in anesthesia; does not point at microtubules.
treatment.strongestObjection: A single four-arm experiment, never repeated, with calculated rather than measured headline values.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Independent replication with directly measured xenon-alone potencies
A magnetic-field-dependence test of the isotope effect

claimAssessments.reasoning: ORCH-E020 reports consciousness-dependent signals. ORCH-E021 (Warren) finds no evidence of entanglement. ORCH-E087 to ORCH-E090 are the authors' quantitative reply: the classical signal could reach at most 0.4% of the initial magnetization, and the predicted correlation distance played no role. The reply is the authors' own, uses formulas derived for chemical solutions, and nobody else has run the sequence.

treatment.plainLanguage: A special MRI technique picks up heartbeat-linked brain signals that fade with sleep, which its authors read as quantum entanglement.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Would show non-classical brain function if validated, but implicates no microtubule.
treatment.strongestObjection: Living tissue has many compartments, and classical effects there can imitate exotic ones (ORCH-E021).
whatWouldChangeOurMind: An independent implementation of the sequence plus phantom validation
A classical mechanism shown to reproduce the signal

claimAssessments.reasoning: ORCH-E017 is a dedicated underground null in Nature Physics, with the model's co-originator as an author. ORCH-E049 is an independent collaboration reaching the same exclusion. ORCH-E019 qualifies what the result means for Penrose, not whether it happened.

treatment.plainLanguage: Underground detectors found none of the faint radiation the simplest gravity-collapse model predicts, ruling that version out.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Excludes one version of the collapse physics, not Penrose's lifetime rule itself.
treatment.strongestObjection: Penrose's criterion is a lifetime relation and predicts no radiation (ORCH-E019).
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A demonstrated flaw in the detectors' background modelling

claimAssessments.reasoning: ORCH-E022 rests the Erdős disproof on an independent mathematician's paper. ORCH-E023 is Lean-verified and peer-reviewed. ORCH-E024 adds officially graded gold. ORCH-E027 records this line's false-positive history, which does not touch these results. ORCH-E025 and ORCH-E026 qualify what the results mean, not whether they happened.

treatment.plainLanguage: AI systems have produced new, checked research mathematics and olympiad gold medals.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Bears on the Gödelian motivation only, not on any microtubule or collapse claim.
treatment.strongestObjection: These are results inside existing frameworks, not the invention of new ones (ORCH-E025).
whatWouldChangeOurMind: Discovery that the Erdős construction was already in the literature

claimAssessments.reasoning: There is one modelling record, ORCH-E044. It fits free parameters to a single hypomagnetic-field experiment that reported no uncertainty, it comes from the same group as the xenon radical-pair work, and it adds no new measurement.

treatment.plainLanguage: A magnetically sensitive chemical reaction may control how fast microtubules assemble.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Would give a quantum route outside Orch OR to the same-direction drug anomaly, with testable field and isotope predictions.
treatment.strongestObjection: A parameter fit to one experiment that reported no uncertainty.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A zinc-isotope difference in microtubule density at matched chemistry
Nulls on both the isotope and the field manipulations

claimAssessments.reasoning: Held on its source statement alone: no admitted evidence record is attached to this claim, so the grade follows the rule for such claims rather than doubt about the paper. The same LISA Pathfinder bound is weighed where its record is attached, on the collapse-physics claim ORCH-C030. The verdict was well_supported before this rule was applied.

treatment.plainLanguage: Spacecraft measurements of free-falling test masses reportedly force the collapse model's cutoff to be larger than any atomic nucleus.

claimAssessments.reasoning: ORCH-E047 reports the null from a peer-reviewed collaboration, with its fit result (6.3 ± 398.8 counts). It constrains white-noise collapse models only.

treatment.plainLanguage: A second, independent underground detector also found no collapse radiation.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: Removes single-experiment doubt about the radiation null, in the same channel.
treatment.strongestObjection: Collapse models with coloured noise evade the bound.
whatWouldChangeOurMind: A signal appearing in a larger exposure

claimAssessments.reasoning: Held on one commentary sentence with no survey behind it; no admitted evidence record is attached. Nothing in the record refutes it either: no rival target-level Meyer–Overton model appears. The related modelling (ORCH-E010) is attached to ORCH-C011, not to this claim.

treatment.plainLanguage: No anesthetic target other than tubulin has a published model that reproduces the classic link between potency and oil solubility.
treatment.diagnosticitySummary: If true, it marks a real gap in the conventional account for inhaled agents.
treatment.strongestObjection: It is asserted by an interested author without any literature survey.

claimAssessments.reasoning: The only attached record, ORCH-E080, is context: it reports yields staying above 0.14 despite the drop, which presupposes the reduction rather than evidencing it. The grade leans on one computational preprint's statement, and is held provisionally with low confidence.

treatment.plainLanguage: Adding realistic molecular disorder to the model sharply cuts the boost from collective light emission.
